title: Proof of work: projects, open source and internships
goal: Create public evidence that you can ship. With few entry-level postings and many applicants, visible work, merged contributions and internships are what move a resume to the top of the pile.
when: Months 4 to 18 (runs alongside the other phases)

steps.title: First Contributions
steps.note: Make your first pull request in a safe sandbox repository.

steps.title: Good First Issue
steps.note: Find beginner-friendly issues in active open-source projects.

steps.title: Build your own X (CodeCrafters list)
steps.note: A catalogue of guided projects: databases, shells, interpreters, git, redis and more.

steps.title: Three merged open-source contributions
steps.brief: Pick one active project whose language you know. Start with documentation or tests, then fix a labelled bug, then a small feature. Follow the contribution guide, respond to review comments and keep the pull requests small.
steps.deliverable: Three merged pull requests with links, plus a note on what review feedback taught you.

steps.title: Ship two projects people can use
steps.brief: Take two of your phase projects (for example the URL shortener and the evaluated RAG app) and make them real: deployed, documented, with a demo link, monitoring and a changelog. Ask two people to use them and record what confused them.
steps.deliverable: Two deployed projects, each with a README that explains the problem, the design trade-offs and measured results.

steps.title: Write three technical posts
steps.brief: Write up a design decision, a debugging story and something you measured. Show numbers and what you got wrong. Publish them where recruiters can find them.
steps.deliverable: Three published posts linked from your GitHub profile and resume.

steps.title: Internship and referral sprint
steps.brief: From your second or third year onward, build a list of 30 target teams, find a real person to message at each (alumni, open-source maintainers, contest peers) and ask for advice before asking for a job. Track replies and follow up.
steps.deliverable: A tracker with outreach dates, replies and the conversations that led to interviews.

exit: Your GitHub profile shows merged contributions, two deployed projects and consistent activity over many months.
A recruiter can find three links (project, post, contribution) that prove you can do the job.
You have had at least five conversations with engineers about their work and have a referral path to your top targets.
